items.headline: Brewers draw first blood — and break the World Series speed record doing it
items.body: Milwaukee edged Tampa Bay 3-2 in Game 1 to go up 1-0. Rookie Jacob Misiorowski opened with a 103.5 mph heater — the fastest pitch in World Series history — and gave up just one run over five innings, while Christian Yelich's early RBI triple set the tone. The Rays loaded the bases in the ninth, but a replay review wiped out a game-ending double play and the Brewers' Trevor Megill had to strike out the last man to survive it.
items.say: Did you catch Game 1? A Brewers rookie threw the fastest pitch in World Series history — 103 and a half. These two little-market teams are putting on a show.

items.headline: El Clásico is back — Real Madrid vs. Barcelona tomorrow at Camp Nou
items.body: The biggest fixture in club soccer returns Sunday: the season's first Clásico between Barcelona and Real Madrid, Matchday 10 at a still-under-renovation Camp Nou. Last time these two met in the league, Barça won it 2-0 to clinch the title — so there's a score to settle and the whole football world will be watching.
items.say: Real Madrid and Barcelona play their first Clásico of the season tomorrow — basically the biggest game in club soccer. You follow any of the European stuff, or just the big ones like this?

items.headline: Korea sweeps, China stumbles — the LPL goes 0-4 on Worlds Swiss Day 1
items.body: The League of Legends Swiss Stage opened with a jolt in Texas: Korea's LCK went a perfect 4-0 in Round 1 while China's mighty LPL was blanked 0-4. Three-time champs T1 dispatched Brazil's LOS in one of the day's fastest games, and Gen.G ground down Invictus Gaming — leaving the sport's traditional superpower on the back foot early.
items.say: The big League of Legends Worlds had a wild first day — Korea won every game and China lost every game, which never happens. Do you follow any esports at all?

items.headline: One win from history — Angel Reese's Dream can clinch the title today
items.body: Atlanta leads the Finals 2-1 and can win it all this afternoon (Game 4, 1 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena). It'd be the first championship in Dream franchise history — against the two-year-old Golden State Valkyries, chasing a title of their own. Angel Reese has been a force on the glass all series; the upstart Valkyries need a win to force the series back to the Bay.
items.say: The WNBA Finals could end today — Angel Reese's Atlanta team is one win from their first-ever title. It's been such a fun underdog series. You catch any of the W this year?

items.headline: Top-5 chaos day — No. 1 Miami hosts Pitt, Ole Miss visits Texas
items.body: A loaded college Saturday: No. 1 Miami puts its ranking on the line at home against Pitt in the noon window, No. 6 Indiana looks to bounce back at Michigan, and the nightcap is a heavyweight — No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas (7:30 ET). Plus Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama. Plenty to keep the couch warm all day.
items.say: Big college football Saturday — the No. 1 team Miami's playing, and Ole Miss at Texas is the night game. You watch any college ball on Saturdays, or just the pros?

items.headline: NFL plays Paris for the first time — plus Chiefs-Seahawks on Sunday night
items.body: Football goes global again: the Steelers and Saints meet in the league's first-ever regular-season game in France on Sunday morning (9:30 a.m. ET from Paris). The late slate brings Packers-Lions, and the primetime marquee is Chiefs at Seahawks on Sunday Night Football — with Cowboys-Eagles capping it all on Monday.
items.say: The NFL's playing its first-ever game in Paris on Sunday morning — wild to think about. Chiefs-Seahawks is the night game. You riding with anybody this season, or just here for the primetime stuff?

items.headline: Olivia Colman orders a husband made of wicker — the oddball 'Wicker' hits theaters
items.body: One of the strangest, most charming films of the fall: Olivia Colman plays a lonely outcast who has a basketmaker (Peter Dinklage) weave her the perfect husband — played, under a full suit of woven prosthetics, by Alexander Skarsgård. It wowed Sundance as an unhinged, tender fairy tale, and it opened in limited release this week ahead of a wide rollout.
items.say: There's this bizarre new movie where Olivia Colman basically has a husband woven out of wicker for her — and people at Sundance loved it. Weirdest premise of the year, right?

items.headline: Fontaines D.C. go cinematic — and pull a 'Stranger Things' star into it
items.body: Irish post-punk favorites Fontaines D.C. are riding high on their new album 'Dopamine Chamber,' and the latest video, 'Japan,' is the one everyone's sharing: a moody, film-like short directed by Luna Carmoon and starring 'Stranger Things' actor Charlie Heaton. If you liked their last record, this one leans even bigger and more atmospheric.
items.say: Fontaines D.C. — the Irish band — put out a new video with the Stranger Things guy, Charlie Heaton, in it. It's really cinematic. You keep up with new music, or stick with what you know?

items.headline: A witchy new mystery for spooky season — 'Yaga' lands on AMC+
items.body: Perfect late-October binge: 'Yaga,' a seductive supernatural thriller starring Carrie-Anne Moss (of 'The Matrix'), premiered this week on AMC+. Built from Kat Sandler's stage play and set in a small coastal town, it spins the old Baba Yaga folklore into eight tight, half-hour episodes of mystery and menace.
items.say: There's a new witchy thriller on AMC+ with Carrie-Anne Moss — the Matrix woman — great Halloween-season watch. You into the spooky stuff this time of year, or does it stress you out?
